Dovish but guarded: The statement highlights strong employment and household spending, yet weak business fixed investment and exports alongside below-target inflation and low market-based inflation compensation. In New Keynesian frameworks, when inflation is below target and expectations are subdued, additional accommodation is warranted to stabilize the output gap (Galí, Gertler, and López-Salido; Svensson), and the Committee’s rate cut and bill purchases align with interest-rate operating procedures emphasized by McCallum and Nelson (1999). The noted weakness in capex is consistent with evidence that investment and inventories are sensitive to internal finance and liquidity conditions (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994), suggesting that easing can cushion real activity in the near term, in line with VAR evidence that monetary shocks affect output (Sims; B. Friedman). Net tone: modestly positive on expansion and labor markets, tempered by soft inflation dynamics and external uncertainties.
